passages.note: Bill overview lists Ortiz as a co-sponsor of HB2721, a statewide law removing municipal zoning limits on middle housing.

passages.provision_quote: The municipality may not do any of the following: 1. Discourage the development of middle housing through requirements or actions that individually or cumulatively make impracticable the permitting, siting, or construction of middle housing.
passages.note: The enacted text bars municipalities from restricting middle housing, matching rung 5's zoning-limit clause.
Final House vote shows Ortiz voting Y on HB2721.

rows.reasoning: Ortiz co-sponsored and voted Y on HB2721 (2024), which bars municipalities from restricting middle housing and voids local zoning limits on it statewide, matching rung 5's clause to 'cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building.' Per the rule that a deregulation law removing the very limits a rung names is on-question but only direction-only, this one bill cannot show that cutting zoning limits is the most she supports, so it cannot establish rung 5 over rungs 3 or 4.
needs_source: Ortiz's own words on whether she supports binding rules (rent caps, required affordable units) or subsidies/tax breaks in addition to this zoning deregulation, to distinguish rung 5 from rungs 3-4
